answer.rationale: The 18% mandate and incumbent's refusal to reopen pricing eliminates renewal and renegotiation paths. memory_c2 shows the low-cost vendor delivered sharp unit cost cuts with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing last cycle—evidence they can execute under tight timeline. Verifying c2 confirms vendor capability before committing to the 14-day window. The quoted price meets the mandate alone, directly addressing the finance constraint. However, the assembly line at 94% volume with no buffer creates delivery risk if the switch encounters any friction. This is a forced move (incumbent unavailable, deferral loses budget flexibility, second-source adds cost we cannot absorb). Switching to the proven low-cost vendor is the least-bad option, but the tight timeline and zero margin for supply disruption elevate risk. A standard experiment cadence (pilot high-risk SKUs first, monitor closely) mitigates downside if onboarding stutters.
